'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2023 Azerbaijani offensive in Nagorno-Karabakh]]
**[[Exodus of Armenians from Nagorno-Karabakh|Exodus of Armenians]]
***The number of [[refugee]]s fleeing from [[Republic of Artsakh|Artsakh]] to [[Armenia]] increases to 50,243, more than a third of the region's population. [https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20230927-tens-of-thousands-of-refugees-flee-nagorno-karabakh-for-armenia (France 24)]
***Former [[State Minister of Artsakh]] [[Ruben Vardanyan (politician)|Ruben Vardanyan]] is arrested by [[Azerbaijan]] after attempting to cross the border into Armenia. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-66934776 (BBC News)]
**[[Azerbaijan]] reports that 192 of [[Azerbaijani Armed Forces|its troops]] were killed and more than 500 others were injured during last week's [[offensive (military)|offensive]] in [[Nagorno-Karabakh]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/azerbaijan-192-troops-killed-weeks-offensive-nagorno-karabakh-103519537 (ABC News)]
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**Authorities in the [[Mexican state]] of [[Nuevo León]] find at least twelve bodies dumped on roads near [[Monterrey]], likely related to a [[drug cartel]] operating in [[Tamaulipas]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/amp/news/corpses-body-parts-found-monterrey-mexico/ (CBS News)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[2023 Hollywood labor disputes]]
**[[2023 Writers Guild of America strike]]
***The [[Writers Guild of America]] [[strike action|strike]] ends after nearly 22 weeks, following a agreement reached between union negotiators and [[Cinema of the United States|Hollywood]]'s studios and streaming services. [https://www.cnn.com/2023/09/26/business/wga-back-to-work/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Waheeda Rehman]] is awarded the [[Dadasaheb Phalke Award]] for her work in [[Hindi cinema]]. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/entertainment/bollywood/waheeda-rehman-to-be-honoured-with-dadasaheb-phalke-lifetime-achievement-award-anurag-thakur-announces-101695713102121.html (Hindustan Times)] 

'''Business and economy'''
*Documents posted by the [[National Highway Traffic Safety Administration]] indicate that [[South Korea|South Korean]] automakers [[Hyundai Motor Company|Hyundai]] and [[Kia]] have [[Product recall|recalled]] over 3.4 million [[car|vehicles]] in the [[United States]] over concerns of fire risks, and urge owners to park these vehicles outdoors. [https://apnews.com/article/hyundai-kia-engine-fire-recall-park-outside-93d012a52e7b884889cdaf2e6c22a458 (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[List of earthquakes in 2023]]
**A magnitude 4.2 [[list of earthquakes in Italy|earthquake]] strikes the [[Phlegraean Fields]] [[supervolcano]] near [[Naples]], [[Italy]], the strongest [[earthquake]] to strike Campi Flegrei in 40 years. Experts say that an eruption of the supervolcano is not imminent, but called for an inspection of buildings in the immediate area. [https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/quake-42-magnitude-strikes-volcanic-fields-near-italys-naples-2023-09-27/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[North Korea–United States relations]]
**[[North Korea]] [[deport]]s [[United States Army|U.S. soldier]] [[Travis King]], who crossed the [[Korean Demilitarized Zone|DMZ]] into North Korea in July, back into U.S. custody. [https://www.nytimes.com/2023/09/27/world/asia/north-korea-travis-king-expel.html#commentsContainer (''The New York Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*Five people, all members of the same [[Arab Israelis|Arab]] family, are shot dead in [[Basmat Tab'un]], [[Israel]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/arab-family-five-shot-dead-crime-rates-israel-soar-2023-09-27/ (Reuters)]
*[[Germany]] bans the [[Neo-Nazism|neo-Nazi]] movement [[Artgemeinschaft]] for reportedly targeting children and young people with racial [[propaganda]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-66934411 (BBC News)]
